Equipment setup for analyzing these reagents in cells and tissues can include imaging with widefield or confocal microscopes and with Structured Illumination Microscopy (SIM) or Stimulated Emission Depletion (STED) microscopy in fixed cells. These fluorescent tracers are also suitable for monitoring rapid regulated changes in living cells that can be captured by live-cell imaging.

Here, we performed live imaging using a Zeiss Observer.Z.1 inverted microscope equipped with Apotome.2, an automated scanning stage, the Zeiss PEECON stage top incubation for Temperature/CO2 for cell culture. Software analyses can be performed across an array of platforms including Imaris or the publicly available and free resource, Image J. Statistical analyses of quantification are best suited for Prism software.

steps.title: Culture and Plate Cells
steps.instruction: Maintain cells at 37 °C in 5 % CO₂ using appropriate medium (RPMI‑1640 or DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS, glutamine and antibiotics). Grow cells in 10‑cm dishes with 10 mL medium per dish. Twenty‑four hours before the assay, detach cells with 0.05 % trypsin, count, and re‑plate:

substeps.instruction: For fixed‑cell imaging: seed 1 mL medium per well onto sterilized 15 mm round coverslips placed in 12‑well plates; aim for 30‑60 % confluency and incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
For live‑cell imaging: seed 0.5 mL medium per well onto 8‑well glass‑bottom chamber slides; incubate 24 h under the same conditions.
Optional: coat coverslips with sterile fibronectin (100 µg/mL, 500 µL per well) for 30 min at room temperature, wash three times with PBS and once with medium before seeding.

steps.title: Prepare Lysosomal Tracer Stocks
steps.instruction: Handle all reagents protected from light and keep aliquots on ice:

substeps.instruction: LysoLive β‑glucosidase substrate: stock 5 mM in Opti‑Klear Live Imaging Buffer; aliquot 2–5 µL, store at –20 °C (stable ≥4 months).
SiR‑Lysosome: dissolve the vial in 50 µL anhydrous DMSO to obtain a 1 mM stock; do not aliquot, store at –20 °C (stable ≥3 months).
LysoSensor dye: stock 1 mM in 50 µL anhydrous DMSO; aliquot as needed, store at –20 °C.
Working concentrations (prepare fresh in culture medium just before use): LysoLive 5–20 µM, SiR‑Lysosome 1 µM, LysoSensor 1–200 µM.

steps.title: Optional Drug or Growth Factor Treatments
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after plating, add the following reagents as required (add a few minutes before or together with lysosomal tracers):

substeps.instruction: GSK3 inhibition: 40 mM LiCl or 8 nM CHIR99021; controls: 40 mM NaCl or DMSO.
Wnt3a stimulation: 100 ng/mL Wnt3a in DMEM; incubate 20 min total with tracer.
Protein synthesis block: 20 µg/mL cycloheximide added ≥4 h before tracer incubation.
Transient transfection: perform 24 h prior to assay using Lipofectamine 2000 per manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Add Lysosomal Tracers to Cells
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate tracer(s) to the culture medium at the working concentrations listed in step 2 (LysoLive 5–20 µM, SiR‑Lysosome 1 µM, LysoSensor 1–200 µM). If performing protein‑degradation or macropinocytosis assays, also add:

substeps.instruction: BSA‑DQ or Ovalbumin‑DQ: 5 µg/mL in DMEM, incubate 30 min.
BSA‑FITC (fluid‑phase marker): 5 µg/mL, same incubation.
TMR‑Dextran 70 kDa: 1 mg/mL, incubate ≤30 min.

steps.title: Incubate Cells with Tracers
steps.instruction: Allow cells to incubate with the tracer‑containing medium for the time recommended for each probe (generally 20–30 min; follow the specific probe’s instructions). Keep cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ and protect from light.

steps.title: Wash and Fix Cells
steps.instruction: After incubation, perform three washes with PBS (0.5 mL per well each). Fix cells by adding 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS (0.5 mL per well) and incubate at room temperature (time not specified; typical 10 min).

steps.title: Immunostaining (Optional Antibody Staining)
steps.instruction: Proceed with the following steps on fixed cells:

substeps.instruction: Wash PBS three times (0.5 mL per well).
Permeabilize with either digitonin 6.5 µg/mL or Triton X‑100 0.15 % in PBS (0.5 mL per well).
Wash PBS three times (0.5 mL per well).
Block for 1 h in blocking buffer (5 % goat serum, 5 % BSA, PBS, sodium azide) (0.5 mL per well).
Incubate primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 1 h at 20 °C, protected from light (0.5 mL per well).
Wash PBS three times (0.5 mL per well).
Incubate secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 40 min at 20 °C (0.5 mL per well).
Wash PBS three times (0.5 mL per well).
Mount coverslips in mounting medium without DAPI.
Dry in the dark at 20 °C for 16 h before imaging.

steps.title: Acquire Fluorescence Images
steps.instruction: Image cells using a widefield or confocal microscope (e.g., Zeiss Observer.Z.1 or Imager.Z1) equipped with appropriate filter sets. Set exposure times between 100–1000 ms (example: 500 ms, light intensity 95 %). Capture at least five Z‑stacks per field and save files as .czi. Acquire multiple random fields (≥10 images per condition) and, if needed, store slides in the dark at 4 °C for up to two weeks.

substeps.instruction: Open .czi files and split channels.
Optional: subtract background with a rolling‑ball radius of 5 pixels (Process → Subtract Background).
Threshold each channel (Image → Adjust → Threshold), select ‘Dark Background’, set ‘Auto’ or adjust manually; record threshold values and apply the same values to all images of the same experiment.
For lysosome area quantification: outline each cell on the DIC image (circle/polygon tool) and measure cell area (Ctrl + M).
Overlay the cell outline onto the binary threshold image and measure lysosomal area (Analyze → Analyze Particles) with size 0‑∞, circularity 0.00‑1.00, ‘Clear Results’ and ‘Summarize’ checked.
Copy lysosome and cell area values into Prism or Excel, compute (lysosome area / cell area) × 100 % for each cell, then average per field.

steps.title: Quantify Lysosomal Parameters and Perform Statistics

substeps.instruction: pH ratio (LysoSensor): acquire both 440 nm (blue) and 540 nm (yellow) emission channels in 16‑bit, subtract background, measure fluorescence intensity per cell in each channel, and calculate the yellow/blue ratio.
Active organelle count: for macropinocytosis, set DIC threshold using MaxEntropy, apply binary watershed, then count particles 0.2–7 µm (circularity –1) with ImageJ’s Particle Analyzer.
Correlate lysosomal fluorescence intensity with vesicle number by plotting intensity versus vesicle count per cell in Prism or Excel.
Colocalization: open paired channels, normalize intensity, run Coloc 2 (Pearson, Manders, Costes, or Li as appropriate).
Statistical analysis: use at least three independent experiments, each with 25–200 cells per condition, analyzed in Prism (two‑tailed t‑test, p < 0.05 considered significant).

description: Lysosomes lie at the crux of a diverse set of diseases (Ballabio and Bonifacino, 2020; Holland et al., 2020; Lawrence and Zoncu, 2019). Recent work highlights a central role for lysosomal catabolic activity in cancer by restoring cellular building blocks and promoting cell growth. Here, we provide simple assays to measure regulated changes of lysosomal function in living cells such as (1) cleavage of a β-Glucosidase fluorogenic substrate (Harlan et al., 2016) (β-glucosidase is the enzyme mutated in Gaucher disease, the most frequent lysosomal storage disease), (2) lysosomal Cathepsin D (using a pepstatin A peptide probe that binds only to the active form of this protease) (Hartsuck, 1976), and (3) lysosome acidification using the ratiometric pH Yellow/Blue LysoSensor dye. Importantly, rapid cellular and metabolic changes can be followed by adding cell-permeable fluorescent reagents to the culture medium without the need for genetic manipulation or overexpression. These protocols have nuances that are carefully described here to help facilitate the application of these reagents to different systems, cell types, and disease models. In sum, these protocols on lysosomal regulation will be useful for studies on regulated protein degradation, cellular metabolism, and cancer (see Albrecht et al., 2020). This protocol is divided into three main sections that will each offer a unique readout for monitoring lysosomal function.
